subject: FedCare: targeted retention carveout & SIG/CAIQ evidence requests
messages:
From: Elena Rojas <erojas@fedcare.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: FedCare Security <security@fedcare.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Targeted retention carveout: session traces / debug snapshots (SIG/CAIQ asks)

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. Our security and compliance team ran a quick review of our SOC 2 / CAIQ mapping and we have a few customer-specific retention asks for FedCare tenant(s). High level: we need temporary carveouts for session traces and ephemeral debug snapshots generated during inference troubleshooting for a small set of tenants. The control owners asked for 3 things from Redwood:

- Mapping of the requested carveout to SIG/CAIQ controls (we need to show why an exception does not weaken compensating controls)
- A concrete evidence bundle you can provide (logs manifest, export proof, deletion certification)
- Confirmation of technical mechanisms to perform targeted deletion and a timeline for producing artifacts

Attached is our internal requirements doc (fedcare_requirements_20270510.pdf) with the specific tenant IDs and a suggested scope. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide per-tenant deletion proof and what artifacts you would produce?

We’re trying to avoid a long legal hold; this is a limited operational carveout for troubleshooting traces only. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the tenant list.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rojas
Senior Security Analyst
FedCare Health

Attachment: fedcare_requirements_20270510.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rojas <erojas@fedcare.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Targeted retention carveout: session traces / debug snapshots (SIG/CAIQ asks)

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear doc. We can support a customer-scoped carveout for troubleshooting artifacts, but to make this audit-ready we typically deliver three things: a retention matrix that enumerates the data types + retention window, a SIG/CAIQ mapping and evidence pack, and a standardized proof-of-deletion certificate once deletion has completed.

Action items I propose from Redwood: 
1) Draft a per-tenant retention matrix (example attached: redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx)
2) Produce an evidence checklist (hash manifests, export logs, S3 object lifecycle records, SOC 2 test artifacts) mapped to the FedCare controls you flagged
3) Provide a deletion certification template and a timeline for the expedited vs full-evidence tracks

To scope this correctly we need the exact impacted tenant IDs (you mentioned a list in the PDF) and whether you prefer an expedited proof (manifest + deletion cert within 5 business days) or a full forensic export (6 weeks). Can you confirm tenant IDs you want in scope and preferred track?

I’ve looped in Neha to drive the evidence pack and Jordan for any product-specific questions (APIs/webhooks for deletion).

Best,
Marcus Lin
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rojas <erojas@fedcare.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Targeted retention carveout: session traces / debug snapshots (SIG/CAIQ asks)

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the note. From an evidence perspective we typically assemble the following artifacts for a scoped retention exception: 

- Retention matrix (per-data-type) with policy IDs and TTLs
- Object manifest (S3 keys + checksums) for any exported traces
- Access logs showing the engineering/CS activity windows (who accessed the export)
- Provenance chain: KV-cache snapshots, service instance IDs, and correlate IDs that map traces to tenant sessions
- Deletion proof: S3 lifecycle records + deletion job logs + optional automated webhook confirmation if your environment supports it

If you want a faster turnaround we can do an expedited track (manifest + deletion cert within 5 business days) with sampling of traces (up to 10% sample) and provide attestations for the rest. The full track (forensic export + full manifest + chain-of-custody) takes ~6 weeks and includes a signed SOC2 evidence supplement.

For either option we’ll need: the tenant list, the earliest and latest event timestamps to include, and whether you require a retention hold start/end date (i.e., temporary carveout window). Send those and we’ll provide a scoped SOW and deliverable dates.

Link to our internal playbook (read-only): https://redwood.sharepoint.com/sites/security/retention-playbook

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Evidence & Controls Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rojas <erojas@fedcare.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Tan <m.tan@fedcare.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Targeted retention carveout: session traces / debug snapshots (SIG/CAIQ asks)

Neha —

Thanks, that is helpful. Confirming scope: tenant ID fc-1423 (production) only; event window 2027-04-20 to 2027-04-30. FedCare prefers the expedited track — we need deletion proof quickly for an upcoming audit.

A couple of clarifying questions: 
1) Does Redwood support a proof-of-delete webhook for hosted tenants, or is that only available for Dedicated/Private customers?
2) For artifacts you referenced (S3 lifecycle records vs deletion job logs), will you provide both or only the manifest + cert? Our auditors typically look for proof that objects are irrecoverable, not just moved to Glacier.
3) Are session traces stored in an immutable bucket for the short window, or do you run a separate purge job that we should expect to see in logs?

If you can confirm the above and commit to the expedited deliverable timeline we’ll lock in fc-1423 for the expedited track. Happy to do a 30-minute call this afternoon if helpful.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachment: -
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rojas <erojas@fedcare.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Targeted retention carveout: session traces / debug snapshots (SIG/CAIQ asks)

Elena —

We can commit to the expedited track for tenant fc-1423 with the following deliverables and clarifications: 

- Deliverables (expedited, target: 5 business days):
  * Object manifest (S3 keys + checksums) for the window you specified
  * Deletion job logs showing the deletion job run and resulting object tombstones
  * S3 lifecycle records and confirmation of non-recoverability (we will include object metadata showing non-versioned deletion where applicable)
  * Signed proof-of-deletion certificate (proof_of_delete_template.docx)

- Webhook/API: for hosted customers we do not currently expose a deletion webhook. We can provide an API-driven deletion request and the artifacts above, and we will log the API call in our audit trail. Webhook delivery is available for Redwood Dedicated/private customers; for hosted customers we will deliver the certificate + signed manifest as the proof artifact.

- Storage/purge model: session traces for hosted tenants are written to short-lived buckets with TTL-controlled lifecycle. For the expedited track we will run a targeted deletion job (non-Glacier tombstone) and provide the deletion logs as evidence. We will not rely solely on Glacier transitions for the proof; deletion job logs + lifecycle records will be provided to demonstrate irrecoverability.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Marcus/Jordan to schedule a 30-minute call today at 15:30 PT to confirm the manifest fields and sign off on the expedited scope
2) FedCare to confirm fc-1423 + your preferred contact for delivery (email for artifacts + any secure transfer preference)
3) Neha will slot the expedited evidence run and confirm ETA after the call

I’ve attached the deletion certificate template and the matrix we’ll use. If that all looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for 15:30 PT.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proof_of_delete_template.docx, redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx
